answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify. Each agent must dock at a public jetty: stake a refundable deposit and complete a verifiable task before it can transact. A hollow profile with no stake or history earns no trust or rewards. Reputation grows only through checkable work: one zephyr of good deeds proves nothing, but sustained useful service does. Faking a thousand identities costs a thousand deposits plus real compute, and slashing forfeits the stake of any identity caught copying or colluding, so attacks cost more than they earn.
